name: Canasta
description: Canasta is a rummy-style partnership card game played with two 52-card decks plus 4 jokers (108 cards). Jokers and 2s are wild. Players form melds of 3+ cards of the same rank. A 'canasta' (meld of 7+ cards) earns powerful bonuses. The game originated in Uruguay in 1939 and became a worldwide phenomenon rivaling Contract Bridge in the 1950s. First partnership to 5000 points wins.

history.origins: Created c.1939 by Segundo Santos (lawyer) and Alberto Serrato (architect) at the Jockey Club of Montevideo, Uruguay. 'Canasta' means 'basket' in Spanish (referring to the discard basket).
timeline: 1939: Created at the Jockey Club of Montevideo, Uruguay.
1940s: Spreads to Argentina and South America.
1950: Rules standardized in North America (Classic Canasta).
1950s: Global crazeâ€”nearly displaces Contract Bridge in popularity.
Present: Two main variantsâ€”Classic Canasta (worldwide) and Modern American Canasta (North America).
history.cultural: A 1950s social phenomenon. Canasta clubs formed internationally. Associated with post-war prosperity and suburban social life in America and Europe.
history.evolution: The 1950 North American codification standardized 11-card deal, discard pile take mechanics, and canasta bonuses. Modern American Canasta (post-1960s) introduced more complex rules around wild cards, red/black threes distinctions, and going-out requirements.

setup.players: 4 in fixed partnerships (partners sit opposite). Variants for 2, 3, or 6.
setup.deck: 108 cards (2Ã—52-card packs + 4 Jokers). Jokers and 2s are wild.
setup.dealing: 11 cards each (Classic). Remainder is stock. Top card turned face-up to start discard pile (if red 3 or wild, bury and turn another).
setup.equipment: Two shuffled 52-card decks + 4 jokers. Score sheet.

rules.objective: Score 5000 points across multiple rounds by building melds, especially canastas (7-card melds).
rules.gameplay: Draw from stock or take discard pile (if top matches meld). Meld 3+ same rank; canasta = 7+ card meld. Jokers and 2s wild. Red 3s: lay face-up, draw replacement. Opening meld: 50/90/120 pts by team score. Go out: meld all, discard last. Target 5000.
keyRules: Initial meld minimum: 0-1499 pts (50 pts min), 1500-2999 pts (90 pts min), 3000+ pts (120 pts min).
Wild cards cannot form a meld by themselves.

strategy.basic: Race to your first canastaâ€”you cannot go out without one. Hoard wild cards; don't waste them on early small melds.
strategy.intermediate: Discard Pile Control: Never discard a card that gives your opponent an easy pile takeback. Coordinate with partner on which ranks to pursueâ€”don't overlap efforts.
strategy.advanced: Freeze the Pile: Discard a wild card (freezing) when opponents are about to take a large pile. Timing of going out is crucialâ€”go out when you maximize your card-point lead and prevent opponent's canastas.
tips: Red threes are pure bonus pointsâ€”lay them immediately and draw.
In the late game, use wild cards to complete your canasta quickly and go out.

variations.name: Modern American Canasta
variations.description: More complex rules, goes-out requirements, and special hands. Dominant in North American clubs.

variations.name: Samba
variations.description: 3 decks. Allows sequence melds (same suit runs). Samba = 7-card run bonus. Target 10000 pts.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Samba uses three decks and sequence melds; engine overrides for deck count and meld types not yet added.

variations.name: Hand and Foot
variations.description: Each player gets 2 sets of cards (the Hand and the Foot). Foot is picked up when Hand is exhausted.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Hand and Foot two-pile structure and pickup rules are not yet modeled as engine overrides.

scoring.description: Card values + canasta bonuses + going out bonus.
scoring.winCondition: First partnership to 5000 points across rounds.

synthesis.shortDescription: Uruguay's 1939 card masterpiece that briefly threatened to dethrone Contract Bridge. Two partnerships race to 5000 points by building melds and completing 7-card canastas with a 108-card double deck.
